correctness.rationale: The monotone weighted occupation A_t makes the exact first-entry event A_t>=C. The two-sided stationary telegraph filter has Beta(q/mu,q/mu) law by the zero-flux stationary equations. The pathwise identity B_t=U_t+exp(-mu t)B_0, with 0<=B_0<=1, gives an all-real-time tail sandwich after centering, without an independence assumption. Beta transformation proves density/Laplace/cumulants and quantile bounds; stochastic moment comparison proves finite-C mean and variance estimates. Exact no-switch clock gives the earliest-time atom. A standalone exact-clock and high-precision checker passed 22808 finite assertions; only the analytic proof establishes the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The physical first-entry problem from outside a bounded active stationary support is directly studied in the motivating 2024 work. A precise nondegenerate far-launch fluctuation distribution, its explicit digamma/trigamma parameters, all-moment limits, fastest-capture atom and sharp-order uniform finite-launch quantile errors answer a mathematically natural question not settled by the known mean. The stochastic sandwich permits reliable finite-initial-distance uncertainty estimates and identifies the physical role of the telegraph switching-to-trap ratio.
